verdict.rationale: Smithery documents a dedicated server page for each listed server where users can discover and try it. It scans servers for metadata, or accepts a static server card. It also generates typed SDKs from each server's tool schemas, and its CLI can search the registry and find tools. Stdio-bundle versus hosted-URL distribution is documented on the publishing side. However, nothing explicitly shows a developer viewing a server's tool list, input schemas, transport, or hosting attributes before connecting. Missing for 10: explicit docs that server pages or the CLI expose tool lists and input schemas before connection, displayed transport and hosting attributes for listed servers, and hands-on corroboration of the pre-connection inspection flow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can inspect a listed server's tools, input schemas, transport, and hosting attributes before connecting to it

citations.quote: Get a dedicated server page where users can discover, try, and install your MCP from any client
you can provide server metadata manually via a static server card at `/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json`
Every MCP server published on Smithery gets a typed TypeScript SDK generated from its tool and trigger schemas.
smithery tool find [query]             # Search tools by name or intent
For local stdio servers — Smithery distributes a pre-built MCPB bundle that clients download and run locally.
